text:
Hannah: hi all, first-day panic 🙃. opened my onboarding PR but both Buildkite and GH Actions are failing. not sure who to @ for repo/app perms.

Jules: welcome! paste the errors and the repo URL and we'll triage. most common is Buildkite GitHub App not having access or the Actions workflow blocked from secrets.

Hannah: repo is github.com/redwood-inference/model-utils (private). Buildkite log shows:
```
install_buildkite_github_app: pipeline cannot access repository (403)
fatal: could not fetch refs
```
GH Actions says:
```
This workflow is not allowed to access secrets. The workflow either comes from a fork or requires approval to access protected environments.
```

buildkite-bot: Buildkite: pipeline "model-utils/onboarding" failed to schedule: github app not configured for repository.

Jules: okay two parallel issues. 1) Buildkite needs the GitHub App installed on that repo or a deploy key set up. 2) GH Actions is blocked by either org policy or environment protection. Are you working from a fork or an in-repo branch?

Hannah: branch is in-repo. I also noticed the workflow file uses runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, build] — I don't think we have a runner with the "build" label in the default pool.

oss-bot: Org policy: "Allow actions and reusable workflows from: Only selected repositories" is enabled. Repos not on the allowlist will not receive org-level secrets.

Marta: quick fixes: I can request the Buildkite app install for model-utils (org admin step) and add you to infra-ci so branch builds are treated as trusted. Also recommend updating the onboarding workflow to ubuntu-latest to avoid self-hosted label mismatches for new hires.

Hannah: sounds great. also FYI the Buildkite agent log later showed a git-lfs smudge error when it tried to fetch some large demo binaries.

Jules: good catch. agents often don't have git-lfs by default. we usually add an install step to the pipeline for onboarding: `sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y git-lfs`.

Marta: requested Buildkite app install and added model-utils to the app scope. I also added Hannah to infra-ci. Jules, can you review the workflow label change?

Jules: pushed a tiny PR that changes runs-on to ubuntu-latest for the onboarding job and adds the git-lfs install step for Buildkite. Also noted the job pushes a test image to ECR — Hannah will need CI role permissions for ECR (ecr:GetAuthorizationToken + ecr:PutImage, etc.) if the pipeline tries to push.

Hannah: I don't have AWS creds locally yet, didn't expect the ECR push on first-run. thanks for the heads up.

buildkite-bot: Build #205 queued — waiting on agent group: general.

Hannah: re-ran GH Action after a maintainer approved the environment access. GH job picked up secrets and passed! :tada:

Jules: Buildkite still failed initially due to git-lfs, but after the small install-step it moved on. final hiccup was a missing IAM role for ECR push; I switched the pipeline to skip the push for onboarding branches, re-run succeeded.

Marta: summary for onboarding doc: 1) Ensure Buildkite GitHub App is installed for the repo or add a deploy key. 2) New hires should branch in-repo until infra-ci membership propagates. 3) Check workflow runner labels and env protections (reviewers block secrets). 4) Install git-lfs on agents or avoid LFS in small sample repos. 5) ECR pushes require CI IAM permissions.

Hannah: build green! thank you all, huge help. looking forward to the CI walkthrough tomorrow. :coffee:
